title: Keep product documentation public under docs/; only planning, pilot and competitive documents live in the private overlay
context: PR #228 moved all 37 files under docs/ to hunch-private and redirected README and site links to the private repository. The npm README, CHANGELOG, ROADMAP and hunchmemory.com/docs then linked to pages a public user cannot open, including the 1.33 upgrade guide for mixed-version deployments and the state contract reference. David chose to restore the public subset before cutting 1.34.0.
decision: Product and reference documentation (state contract, state CLI, TypeScript and Python clients, upgrade guides, task reports, Project DNA, change proof, engineering landscape, review memory, agent origin, autonomy ladder, cookbook, MCP registry, guard review, observation contracts, ledger reuse, behavior-policy recovery, development preparation, state-recall evaluation) is tracked in the public repository under docs/ and linked relatively. Planning, pilot and competitive documents (competitive-landscape, outreach-pipeline, next-release-memory-impact, autonomous-development, external-acceptance-runbook, task-report-qualification, outcome-experience-protocol, evidence/) stay in hunch-private/projects/hunch/docs and public files link to them by absolute private URL. The /docs/ gitignore rule is removed.
consequences: Public README, CHANGELOG, ROADMAP and site links to product docs resolve again for users without private access.
Public files still carry a few links into the private repository for internal documents; those 404 for outsiders by design.
A document is either public or private, never both; moving one is a deliberate change with a link sweep.
alternatives_rejected: Rewrite every public link to drop docs/ entirely: loses the upgrade guide and contract spec for users.
Keep all docs private and accept broken public links: ships an npm README that points at 404s.

premises.claim: The public upgrade guide exists in this repository
